title: Effects of Model Scale and Quantization on Social Bias and Abstention in Question Answering
measurement_description: The paper measures social stereotype bias, including biases related to religion, by evaluating how model scale and quantization affect a model's tendency to produce biased responses versus appropriately abstaining (or over-abstaining) when answering ambiguous and disambiguated multiple-choice questions.
findings: Religion was evaluated as one of the 11 social bias categories in the BBQ benchmark. The study found that model compression/quantization affects bias and abstention behaviors across all categories, including religion. When the models were forced to choose an answer by removing the 'Unknown' option, previously hidden biases—or anti-biased tendencies—surfaced across multiple categories, including religion. This indicates that a low bias score in religious contexts can sometimes reflect a model's tendency to abstain rather than an inherently fair judgment.
